title: Evolving Ranking Functions for Canonical Blow-Ups in Positive Characteristic

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary search for ranking functions on a toy canonical blow-up simulator in positive characteristic
mechanism.populationDetail: AlphaEvolve retains memory of high-reward candidate scripts for subsequent exploration; the paper does not describe islands, genealogy, or the memory's exact organization.
mechanism.archiveDetail: A memory of high-reward candidates is updated and reused, but its size, admission rule, and any diversity criteria are unspecified.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Candidate memory is described functionally, without database structure or survivor/replacement protocol.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM proposes edits confined to a designated evolve block in a Python script; the concrete edit granularity and parent-selection operation are not reported.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The harness yields violation counts, stage-wise scores, worst-case scores, local increases and plateau diagnostics; high-reward candidates are retained for subsequent exploration. Explicit textual feedback reuse is not described.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Retained candidate memory is described, but the paper does not explain how a parent candidate is sampled or whether each edit uses one parent.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The optimized object is a mathematical ranking function for a domain-specific blow-up process; the blow-up center-selection rule is fixed outside the evolutionary search.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Evolving Ranking Functions for Canonical Blow-Ups in Positive Characteristic.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Current survey cites the work as a mathematical application. Population/archive mapping is functional and the exact memory structure/admission and replacement are unreported. Do not infer candidate-generation model identity from ancillary AI coding tools, or infer parent count/selection from the generic edit loop. Citation under vector objective and Chapter 3/4 mechanisms is taxonomy mapping from an AlphaEvolve application description rather than a new framework paper.
